title: Bacon Potato Cake
description:
Oh my, this is so good, it’s almost sinful! The recipe for this “heavenly” treat appeared in the New York Times in February 2000 – what a way to start off the new millennium. The article began with the quote, “Sin is in, gastronom-ically speaking,” with the author pursuing “post-graduate studies in bacon.” I’d surely give him a Ph.D. for this recipe.
Like the author, I love bacon, though I know we’re not supposed to eat that much. Usually, I buy good bacon and then trim as much fat as I can by hand. It’s a little more work this way, but way better than buying “hand trimmed” bacon at the store.
No matter what you do, this is an amazing dish, not only the way it tastes, but also the way it looks.
Is the “smoky trail to bacon” like the “bumpy road to love?”
Both end up wonderful!
START TO FINISH: 1 ½ HOURS
Bacon-Potato Cake
Preheat oven to 425 degrees.
Lightly butter a 10-inch skillet or other oven-proof roundish pan.
Pat the peeled and sliced potatoes dry on paper towels. Place them in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Line the skillet with bacon slices, starting each in the middle of the pan and arranging them like spokes of a wheel and slightly overlapping. Let the ends hang over the edge of the pan.
Arrange one-third of the potatoes in the pan in an even layer. Top with half the cheese.
Add half the remaining potatoes, then the rest of the cheese, then the rest of the potatoes.
Fold the overhanging bacon strips back over the top.
Place the pan on the lowest rack in the oven, and bake 45 to 50 minutes, until the potatoes offer no resistance when pierced with the point of a sharp knife.
Use a spatula to compress the cake a few times during baking.
Cool the cake on a rack for a few minutes. Place a serving plate over the cake, and invert.
Serve in wedges.
ingredients: 3 pounds Idaho potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
16 slices (not thick) slab bacon, about 8 ounces
8 ounces Gruyere cheese, shredded butter for pan
